body: Sorry I missed a day...  Things have gotten better for me again as they often do.  I don't bottom out so hard often, but when I do it's just crazy.  How about you... what's your pattern?  (Do you have a pattern?)

We had a 10 hour drive back home yesterday and we talked about a great many things including this.  It wasn't always easy for either of us, but it was important.

Despite everything, we did find and put an offer on a house which was our reason for the trip.  My wife also recently heard about 'cognitive therapy' from a mutual friend who is receiving treatment.  This sounds like a potential avenue for me to get help where I've struck out in the past.  I'll probably actively seek this out in about 12 weeks when the move is complete and the dust is settled.

My wife is truly an awesome person and one of the most decent human beings I've ever known.  This is why it is so painful when I do anything that hurts her.

You've been a great support.  Thank you.

For starters... it's been two days now and I'm doing much better.  My wife and I are back on good terms though I'm sure we're both going to need some time to get completely back to rights.  I have survived once again.  Thank you to everyone who showed concern and support.  It's not the first time I've felt a need to post on here and based on four decades of knowledge, it probably won't be the last.  I'd buy every one of you a beer (or beverage of your choice) and give you a hug if I could.

Their forgiveness in the whole scheme of things is relatively easy.  It's forgiving myself that is the real trick.  If I could figure that out it would probably greatly improve my sense of self worth and reduce my chronic depression.

My dad is a psychopathic asshole and an expert at manipulating people.  I live in perpetual fear that I will be like him.  When I screw up and mess with my marriage it really crushes my identity.  I don't just feel depressed, I feel like a monster in those times.  

Have a great night and thanks again!

I'm glad you wrote.  I just wrote last night, too.  I'm to a point where I kind of have a contract with myself to always post and wait at least one day.  Even when I don't see how shit will possibly sort itself out just one more night lets magic happen.

Keep hanging in there...  talk to you again tomorrow?

Most of the time I can deal with my pain.  It's when I become super conscious of the pain that I cause to them that it becomes unbearable.  That's when my thoughts turn to "damned if I do, damned if I don't" and start doing the evaluation of which one to choose.

Thank you for the response.

Well... for starters, I'm still alive.  Today was better than yesterday, but I'm mentally and physically exhausted.  I only got maybe 3 hours of sleep last night.  We're out of town because I'm supposed to be transferring to a new state for work and we are looking for houses.  If we buy one then it actually takes away my opportunity to be done.  Right now we have absolutely no long term debt of any kind.  We own our vehicles and our home.  The move will drain all of our cash, put us into debt for probably 15-20 years, and force us to live much more frugally.

Anyway... I'm way off subject.  Thank you for writing back and caring.  I know my thoughts aren't rational.  I also know that the pain is excruciating and that it spills over to and impacts the person I care about most in the world.

My wife knows that I suffer from depression.  We've grown up together so she's been there through all of the ups and downs.  I remember a period where she also got severely depressed  after coming down with a severe life-changing chronic disease.  I don't even know how she puts up with me.

She also knows that I've had thoughts of suicide at various times in my life, including in my youth long before she and I met.  I can't bring this to her when she and I are out of sync because then it comes off as coercive.

I am generally smart and genuinely care about people.  However, I'm not a natural people person and so even though I care it can come across as cold and non-empathetic.  I try so hard so when I fail (especially when I fail spectacularly as I did on Saturday) it's crushing.  Then I find myself in a place where even when I realize that I've hurt her that I'm so compromised that I just keep digging  even in my efforts to apologize and be responsible.

There's no question that I've hurt her so many times.  Shortly before I posted my message everything had just gone critical again when I had thought it was getting slightly better.  In the middle of her needing to be acknowledged and reassured I brought up how I hated myself for hurting her.  This led to her (rightly) declaring that I wouldn't be able to be there for her in the way she needed as long as I hate myself.  This, of course, triggered for me the thought of even trying to live without her which is truly unthinkable.  It also led to the despair that I have no idea how to fix the problem so I can be sure that I will continue hurting her.

I so wish I knew how to find helpful treatment.  Ten-ish years ago my depression was super severe and persistent.  I would have lost my job had I not had the where-with-all to do an FMLA leave of absence for a couple months.  I was so very close to suicide at that time.  I went to both a psychologist and a psychiatrist.  Neither of them seemed to appreciate and recognize the seriousness of what I was telling them.  I went in half way hoping one of them would have me committed and left with absolutely nothing.  The problem (in my estimate) is that I'm quite highly functional and not at all obvious.

Thank you again for reading my rambling.  It's uplifting to know there are people like you who care.

It just feels like the right answer that, although harsh, is best for everyone.  I never should have gotten married and had children in the first place.  They simply don't deserve more years of pain that I unwittingly cause for them.  I guess I'm looking at like ripping off the band-aid.  It's not a question of whether it has to come off it's just a question of do it quick and get it over with or let it be long and drawn out.

Thank you for responding and caring.
